_comment: THE ARTIFACT INVENTORY — every record the scoped application is made of,
WHAT THIS IS FOR. Until now the application's parts were enumerated across
three documents and a directory listing, and nothing checked that the four
agreed. test/packaging.test.js now does: a Script Include added to src/ and
not listed here fails, a property documented in records/properties.md and
not listed here fails, and a property listed here that LucairnConfig does
not know fails. The inventory and the code cannot drift apart quietly.
WHAT THIS IS NOT. It is NOT an update set, and it is not an installer.
There is no sys_remote_update_set_*.xml in this repository and there will
not be one until an instance produces it: an update-set XML that names one
field wrong imports silently wrong, so a hand-written one would be a guess
dressed up as an artefact. README.md § Export the update set is the path —
you BUILD the app once on an instance, from these sources and the record
specifications, and export the set from there.
Nothing listed here has been created on a ServiceNow instance.

scope.note: ServiceNow assigns the scope prefix when the application is created; it will not be this one. Every scoped name below carries the placeholder and must be substituted.

artifacts.name: lucairn.now_assist.api_key
artifacts.note: Type must be password2, not string. Never travels inside an update set.

artifacts.name: lucairn.now_assist.vendor
artifacts.spec: src/records/properties.md § lucairn.now_assist.vendor has no default, on purpose
artifacts.note: No default, on purpose. Unset means every protected run is blocked. The accepted set is the Lucairn service's own contract — extending it is a separate design pass, not a configuration choice.

artifacts.name: lucairn.now_assist.output_destination
artifacts.write_authority: x_lcrn_now_assist_admin only — a recognised-but-wrong value silently un-protects every run, so this is a privacy control, not a tuning knob (verification item V6).

artifacts.name: skill policy + evidence table access control
artifacts.note: Specified, not suggested, and NOT yet verified. An unverified ACL row is not a control.

artifacts.name: synthetic incidents
artifacts.spec: README.md § Build on the PDI, step 6
artifacts.note: Synthetic only. Every fixture email sits on a reserved .test domain that cannot resolve, and a unit test asserts it.

not_included.why: Nothing here has executed on an instance. A hand-written update set that names one field wrong imports silently wrong — it would be a guess dressed up as an artefact. The set is EXPORTED from the first instance build (README.md § Export the update set) and committed then, with the instance family and patch level in the commit message.

not_included.artifact: an installer or automated deployment path
not_included.why: The build procedure is a human one against an instance, and every mechanism it depends on is an unproven hypothesis (contracts/instance-contracts.json). Automating an unverified procedure would only make it fail faster.
